audioBrief.headline: The Swiss Franc Fortress: Why Currency Strength Shields Without Suffocating Exporters
audioBrief.script: Good day. In an era of persistent global inflationary pressure, the Swiss Franc continues to confound conventional economic theory. While a surging exchange rate traditionally harms export competitiveness, Swiss manufacturers have leveraged high-value specialization to preserve operating margins. The NZZ analyzes the Swiss National Bank's balance-sheet strategy and the institutional roots of monetary stability. For the Neue Zürcher Zeitung, Falkenstrasse Zurich.

executiveNewsletter.headline: The Franc's Double Armor
executiveNewsletter.subhead: How imported disinflation counterbalances real effective exchange rate appreciation
bullets: The Swiss Franc gained 4.8% on a trade-weighted basis against major partner currencies over the past 18 months.
Imported goods inflation fell to negative 0.4%, neutralizing energy and commodities cost pressures on households.
Precision machinery, pharmaceuticals, and luxury watchmaking maintained gross export revenues above CHF 260 billion.

slides.headline: The Two Pillars of Resilience
slides.bodyText: Why the textbook economic dogma of currency devaluation fails in the Swiss context.

card1.title: INELASTIC PRICING POWER
card1.text: Specialized pharmaceuticals, precision medtech, and luxury horology possess low price elasticity, enabling exporters to pass on high nominal prices.

card2.title: ENERGY IMPORT RELIEF
card2.text: Denominated in stronger francs, imported crude oil, natural gas, and intermediate industrial inputs cost substantially less at Swiss borders.

items.question: Does a strong Franc hurt Swiss manufacturing competitiveness?
items.answer: Traditional price-sensitive manufacturing experiences margin compression, but the Swiss export sector has shifted toward high-margin pharmaceuticals, medtech, and luxury goods with high pricing inelasticity.

items.question: Why doesn't the SNB target a weaker exchange rate to stimulate growth?
items.answer: Artificial devaluation imports foreign inflation, erodes domestic purchasing power, and balloons central bank foreign currency exposure without yielding sustainable industrial productivity gains.

items.question: What long-term policy stance does the NZZ advocate?
items.answer: Uncompromising monetary price stability paired with liberal structural labor markets, minimal state industrial intervention, and sustained investment in vocational and university research.
